summary: Kaniama territory (Haut-Lomami) has no reported armed-group control; Mai-Mai/Bakata Katanga activity in 2025-2026 was concentrated in Bukama, Malemba-Nkulu, Mitwaba and Pweto, and the province was reported calm in September 2026. Kaniama town is a state-run territorial centre with permanent PNC and FARDC presence and received a presidential visit in late July 2026. The Kaniama-Kasese site west of town hosts the Service National training and re-education centre (former kuluna and youth) and its agro-industrial domain, run by the paramilitary Service National. Rural villages are assessed as default state presence (PNC).

new_entities.name: Service National (RDC)
new_entities.description: Paramilitary national service under the presidency that runs civic/re-education training centres and agricultural domains (notably Kaniama-Kasese); controller only at its own sites.

zones.evidence: Kaniama is a calm, state-administered territorial centre; it hosted a presidential visit in July 2026 and the province was reported calm in September 2026, with armed-group activity limited to Bukama/Malemba-Nkulu/Mitwaba. Policing by PNC with FARDC and intelligence services present.

zones.description: Kaniama-Kasese area (Kasese health area: Kasese Poste, Agri) – Service National training centre and agro-industrial domain
zones.evidence: The Kaniama-Kasese centre, relaunched in 2020, is run by the paramilitary Service National, which trains and re-educates thousands of youths (including former kuluna) and handles discipline on site; a soldier-worker altercation there in April 2026 was handled by military justice. Control over the surrounding villages (vs. PNC) is inferred.

zones.description: Rural Kaniama territory (all other villages, incl. Tshilayi, Kafuyage, Kipanga, Musaka, Muleba, Hamba border area)
zones.evidence: No reports of armed-group presence or control in Kaniama territory in 2025-2026; Mai-Mai incursions in Haut-Lomami are reported in Bukama, Malemba-Nkulu, Mitwaba and Pweto. Default state presence (PNC posts, customary chiefs).
